import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    postings = inputs["POSTINGS"].copy()

    # Preserve stable ordering by account_id, post_date, post_seq
    postings = postings.sort_values(
        by=["account_id", "post_date", "post_seq"],
        kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    qty = postings["qty"]
    unit_price = postings["unit_price"]

    valid_mask = (
        qty.notna() & (qty > 0) &
        unit_price.notna() & (unit_price >= 0)
    )

    posted = postings.loc[valid_mask].copy()
    posted["post_value"] = posted["qty"] * posted["unit_price"]
    posted["running_total"] = posted.groupby("account_id")["post_value"].cumsum()

    posted_totals = posted[
        ["account_id", "post_seq", "post_date", "post_value", "running_total"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

    # Reject counts: count invalid rows per account
    reject_rows = postings.loc[~valid_mask]
    reject_counts_series = reject_rows.groupby("account_id").size()

    # All accounts present in POSTINGS must appear, even with zero rejects
    all_accounts = postings["account_id"].drop_duplicates()
    # Preserve the order accounts first appear (matching cursor's account transition order)
    seen_order = postings["account_id"].drop_duplicates().tolist()

    reject_counts = pd.DataFrame({"account_id": seen_order})
    reject_counts["reject_count"] = reject_counts["account_id"].map(
        reject_counts_series
    ).fillna(0).astype(int)

    return {
        "posted_totals": posted_totals,
        "reject_counts": reject_counts
    }
